text.p: Italian bonds futures slipped back from new record highs set in early trade as weakness in overseas bond markets undermined the current wave of optimism in Italian debt markets, dealers said.

The LIFFE December contract touched a new record high of 128.58 driven by optimism over Italy's imminent entry to the ERM, the strengthening lira, and Tuesday's acceptance of the government's new Euro-tax package by Italy's trade unions.
However, bund weakness and lower T-bonds undermined by the weak dollar caused BTP contract to pulled back from the highs as investors turned a fraction cautious.

Dealers said that investors are now looking for preliminary November CPI figures to be issued over the next two days. Market expectations are for a decline to around 2.6 percent from October's 3.0 percent, but some dealers are looking for 2.5 percent with an interest rate cut soon following.

Six Italian cities are due to publish their CPI data after 1630 GMT on Thursday and the remaining four on Friday. Dealers said that a lower CPI rate may prompt an interest rate cut, or if not in December after that month's preliminary figures.
"The interest rate cut story is still strong, and is keeping the market bubbling away," said one dealer.

Dealers added that the current correction could only be temporary with many investors long of the market awaiting the lira's ERM entry, lower inflation and watching the lira's rise today which came despite dollar weakness.
